chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hadeed who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Fear Allah, and maintain your religion with piety (al-wara'), and strengthen it with dissimulation (al-taqiyyah) and self-sufficiency with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, whoever humbles himself to the ruler and to those who oppose him in his religion, seeking what is in their hands for his worldly life, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will suppress him and detest him, and leave him to himself. If he succeeds in securing something from his worldly life, and something from it comes to him, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is His Name, will remove the blessings from it, and will not recompense him for anything he spends on Hajj, nor freeing a neck, nor righteousness.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Dissimulation or prudence in concealing faith
key_terms.الْوَرَعِ: Piety or scrupulousness in religious matters

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of humbling oneself to rulers for worldly gain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of al-Kulayni’s chapter on political authority, this hadith establishes a theological framework for navigating power dynamics, linking spiritual integrity (wara') and strategic dissimulation (taqiyyah) to divine protection. It warns that compromising faith for worldly gain leads to Allah's rejection (maqatahu) and the nullification of major acts of worship, such as Hajj and manumission, emphasizing that political submission for material benefit invalidates spiritual merit.
